title: Delocalizing a resolution at a prime of height zero
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $A$ an $R$-algebra of finite presentation, $A\to\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras and $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ a prime ideal, with $\mathfrak h_A=\sqrt{H_{A/R}\Lambda}$ as in [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be the inverse image of $\mathfrak q$, $R_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ the localizations [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $A_{\mathfrak p}=A\otimes_RR_{\mathfrak p}$ (of finite presentation over $R_{\mathfrak p}$, with the induced map $A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$). Assume (1) $\mathfrak q$ is minimal over $\mathfrak h_A$; (2) $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}\supset\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ can be resolved [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]; (3) $\dim\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}=0$ (Krull dimension: every prime ideal of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is maximal, i.e. $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is its only prime). Then $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$ can be resolved.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero, line 2230), Section 07F6 (section-local)

proof.text: (Generators of $H_{A/R}$.) $A$ is of finite presentation, in particular of finite type, over the Noetherian ring $R$, hence $A$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], so the ideal $H_{A/R}\subset A$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]: $H_{A/R}=(a_1,\dots,a_r)$ with $r\ge0$ (if $r=0$ read the constructions below with no $y_i$, $t_{ij}$).

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), line 2252 ('Say H_{A/R} = (a_1, ..., a_r)')

proof.text: (The element $\lambda$ and the exponent $N$.) By (1), $\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution], so $\alpha(a_i)\in\mathfrak q$ for all $i$. $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; by (3) every prime of $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is maximal, so $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is its only prime ideal, and $\sqrt{0}=\bigcap_{\mathfrak P\in V(0)}\mathfrak P=\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ in $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq]. Hence each $\alpha(a_i)/1$ is nilpotent; take $N\ge1$ with $(\alpha(a_i)/1)^N=0$ for all $i$. By the definition of the localization there are $\lambda_i\in\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $\lambda_i\alpha(a_i)^N=0$ in $\Lambda$; $\lambda=\lambda_1\cdots\lambda_r\notin\mathfrak q$ ($\mathfrak q$ prime; $\lambda=1$ if $r=0$) satisfies $\lambda\alpha(a_i)^N=0$ for all $i$. (Stacks says $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ is Artinian, hence $\mathfrak q\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ nilpotent and $\lambda(\mathfrak h_A)^N=0$; $\Lambda$ is not assumed Noetherian, so only the elementwise nilpotence written here holds, and it is all the proof uses.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), lines 2245-2253

proof.text: (The intermediate algebra $C$.) By (1), (2) and [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-weak] (Stacks 07F9) there is a factorization $A\xrightarrow{\beta}C\xrightarrow{\gamma}\Lambda$ of $\alpha$ by $R$-algebra maps, $C$ of finite presentation over $R$, with $H_{C/R}\Lambda\not\subset\mathfrak q$; since this ideal is generated by $\gamma(H_{C/R})$, there is $c\in H_{C/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] with $\gamma(c)\notin\mathfrak q$. $C$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by the images of finitely many $R$-algebra generators, so it is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $A$ (Step 1), hence of finite presentation over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]: fix $C=A[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with $\beta$ the structure map, and choose $p_c\in A[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with class $c$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), lines 2254-2256

proof.text: (The algebra $B$ and the map $B\to\Lambda$.) Put $B=A[x_1,\dots,x_n,y_1,\dots,y_r,z,t_{ij}]/(f_j-\sum_iy_it_{ij},\ zy_i)$, $t_{ij}$ being $rm$ variables ($1\le i\le r$, $1\le j\le m$) [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. $B$ is generated as an $R$-algebra by the images of finitely many $R$-algebra generators of $A$ and the classes of the variables, so it is of finite type over the Noetherian ring $R$, hence of finite presentation over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation]. Define the $A$-algebra map $\delta:B\to\Lambda$ by $x_k\mapsto\gamma(\bar x_k)$, $y_i\mapsto\alpha(a_i)^N$, $z\mapsto\lambda$, $t_{ij}\mapsto0$ (with $A\to\Lambda$ equal to $\alpha=\gamma\beta$): it is well defined because $f_j-\sum_iy_it_{ij}\mapsto\gamma(\bar f_j)=0$ and $zy_i\mapsto\lambda\alpha(a_i)^N=0$ (Step 2). (This is Stacks' composite $B\to C[y_i,z]/(y_iz)\to\Lambda$, $t_{ij}\mapsto0$.) Thus $A\to B\xrightarrow{\delta}\Lambda$ is a factorization of $\alpha$ by $R$-algebra maps, and, writing $c'\in B$ for the class of $p_c$, $\delta(c')=\gamma(c)$, $\delta(zc')=\lambda\gamma(c)\notin\mathfrak q$ and $\delta(a_\ell y_\ell)=\alpha(a_\ell)^{N+1}$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), lines 2256-2264

proof.text: ($zc'$ lies in $H_{B/R}$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-height-zero-auxiliary-algebra-localizations] (1), $B_z\cong C[t_{ij},z]_z$ as $A$-algebras, with $c'\mapsto c$. $C\to C[t_{ij},z]$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth], and so is $C\to C[t_{ij},z]_z$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]. Base change along $C\to C_c$ gives that $C_c\to C_c\otimes_CB_z\cong(B_z)_c$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] is smooth, and $R\to C_c$ is smooth because $c\in H_{C/R}$ [lem-weil-pbc-singular-ideal-localization-smooth]; so the composite $R\to(B_z)_c$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition]. Finally $(B_z)_{c'}\cong B_{zc'}$ as $B$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], so $B_{zc'}$ is a smooth $R$-algebra and $zc'\in H_{B/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. (Stacks writes $B_z\cong C[y_1,\dots,y_r,z,z^{-1}]$ 'hence smooth', and concludes $z\in H_{B/R}$; but $C$ is not smooth over $R$, and the correct statement is $zc'\in H_{B/R}$ for $c\in H_{C/R}$, which is what the conclusion needs.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), lines 2266-2268, 2271-2273

proof.text: ($a_\ell y_\ell$ lies in $H_{B/R}$.) Fix $\ell$. By [lem-weil-pbc-popescu-height-zero-auxiliary-algebra-localizations] (2), $B_{y_\ell}\cong(Q_\ell)_{y_\ell}$ with $Q_\ell=A[x_k,y_i,t_{ij}\,(i\ne\ell)]$ as $A$-algebras; $A\to Q_\ell$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] and so is $A\to(Q_\ell)_{y_\ell}$ [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]. Base change along $A\to A_{a_\ell}$: $A_{a_\ell}\to A_{a_\ell}\otimes_AB_{y_\ell}\cong(B_{y_\ell})_{a_\ell}$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor] is smooth; $R\to A_{a_\ell}$ is smooth as $a_\ell\in H_{A/R}$ [lem-weil-pbc-singular-ideal-localization-smooth]; so $R\to(B_{y_\ell})_{a_\ell}$ is smooth [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] ('compositions of smooth maps are smooth'). As $(B_{y_\ell})_{a_\ell}\cong B_{a_\ell y_\ell}$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], $a_\ell y_\ell\in H_{B/R}$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), lines 2269-2273

proof.text: (Conclusion.) With $\mathfrak h_B=\sqrt{H_{B/R}\Lambda}$ formed with $\delta$ [def-weil-pbc-popescu-resolution]: $\delta(zc')=\lambda\gamma(c)\in H_{B/R}\Lambda\setminus\mathfrak q$ (Steps 4, 5), so $\mathfrak h_B\not\subset\mathfrak q$; and $\alpha(a_\ell)^{N+1}=\delta(a_\ell y_\ell)\in H_{B/R}\Lambda$ (Steps 4, 6), so $\alpha(a_\ell)\in\mathfrak h_B$ for every $\ell$, hence $H_{A/R}\Lambda=(\alpha(a_1),\dots,\alpha(a_r))\subset\mathfrak h_B$ and, $\mathfrak h_B$ being radical, $\mathfrak h_A\subset\mathfrak h_B$. With $B$ of finite presentation over $R$ (Step 4), $A\to B\xrightarrow{\delta}\Lambda$ is a resolution of $R\to A\to\Lambda\supset\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07FA (lemma-delocalize-height-zero), lines 2264-2275 ('We claim that B is a solution ... This proves the lemma')

split_report.summary: Wrote the proof of Stacks 07FA (smoothing.tex 2245-2275) in 7 steps. The proof cites only Lemma 07F9 (lemma-delocalize-weak), not 07F4 (delocalize-base), 07CT (desingularize-strictly-standard), Ogoma or strictly standard elements as the brief guessed; new unsplit nodes: lem-weil-pbc-popescu-delocalize-weak (07F9) and lem-weil-pbc-popescu-height-zero-auxiliary-algebra-localizations (the two isomorphisms B_z = C[t,z]_z and B_{y_l} = A[...]_{y_l} that Stacks asserts). Existing tools used: finite-type-algebra-noetherian, finite-type-noetherian-finite-presentation, zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq, singular-ideal-localization-smooth, polynomial-ring-smooth, smooth-ring-map-principal-localization, smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition, localization-tensor, localization-of-localization. Corrections to Stacks: (a) Lambda_q is only zero-dimensional local, not Artinian (Lambda arbitrary), so only each a_i^N dies, which suffices; (b) B_z is C[t_ij,z,z^{-1}], not C[y_i,z,z^{-1}], and it is smooth over C, not over R: z is not shown to be in H_{B/R}; z c' with c in H_{C/R}, gamma(c) not in q, is, and maps outside q; (c) the inclusion h_A in h_B (part of 'resolved') is derived from a_l y_l -> alpha(a_l)^{N+1}. Statement unchanged except that dim = 0 is spelled out; def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal added to stmt_deps (H_{A/R} is in the statement).

reviewed.note: 7 steps follow Stacks 07FA with three corrections written into the steps: Lambda_q need not be Artinian (only elementwise nilpotence of the alpha(a_i) is used), B_z = C[t_ij, z]_z (Stacks' C[y, z, z^{-1}] is a misprint) so the element in H_{B/R} is zc' with c in H_{C/R} rather than z, and h_A subset h_B derived from a_l y_l. New nodes: 07F9 (delocalize-weak) and the two localization isomorphisms of B. L checked the isomorphisms and the smoothness chains. Tags 07FA, 07F9 verified.
